title: Recurrences and Compositions (playlist gap)
quickIdea: When a structure is built by adding one step to a smaller structure, count by a recurrence. This topic is in the GATE syllabus but is not taught by this playlist.
remember: Compositions of n into 1s and 2s satisfy f(n) = f(n-1) + f(n-2) with f(1) = 1, f(2) = 2 - the Fibonacci shift.
Number of compositions of n into parts 1 and 2 is F(n+1) with F(1) = F(2) = 1.
All compositions of n (any part sizes) number 2^(n-1).
Generating function for compositions into 1s and 2s: 1/(1 - x - x^2).

example.prompt: Number of 10-pennants (sequences of 1s and 2s summing to 10).

gateAngle: GATE CS 2014 Set 1 Q.49 (answer 89) is this exact computation. Because the playlist does not teach recurrences, treat this as a flagged gap and revise it separately.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: How many compositions of 6 use only the parts 1 and 2?
variations.why: f(6) = 13 from the same recurrence. Cross-check by the stars-and-bars style count: compositions with j twos contribute C(6-j, j) and summing over j = 0..3 gives 1 + 5 + 6 + 1 = 13.

trap.what: Using 2^(n-1) when the allowed parts are restricted.
trap.why: 2^(n-1) counts compositions with any part sizes. Restricting the parts to 1 and 2 gives Fibonacci growth instead.
trap.counterexample: For n = 5: all compositions = 16, compositions using only 1 and 2 = 8.

check.question: How many compositions of 5 use only 1s and 2s?
